tagline.en: From a model that runs to a service that survives rush hour: optimization, high-concurrency serving with vLLM, multi-GPU, Kubernetes and LLMOps — measured every week on a public leaderboard.

audience.en: ML / LLM engineers, MLOps, DevOps and backend engineers

format.en: 15 topics · each one a lecture + a hands-on seminar

workload.en: ≈ 10–14 hours per week, ≈ 150–200 hours in total

goal.en: Train an engineer who can optimize an LLM, stand up a high-performance OpenAI-compatible API on vLLM, serve dozens to hundreds of concurrent clients from a single instance, deploy the system on multiple GPUs and Kubernetes, and operate it as LLMOps.

outcomes.en: Explain where inference time and memory go — prefill vs decode, the KV cache, memory bandwidth — and predict the bottleneck before measuring it.
Quantize a model and defend the speed / memory / quality trade-off with numbers.
Serve a model through vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API and tune it for a given concurrency profile.
Benchmark a serving stack honestly: throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p95, failures — under 1 to 128+ concurrent clients.
Package, deploy and scale inference: Docker, tensor parallelism, Kubernetes with GPU Operator and HPA.
Operate it: metrics, dashboards, alerts and cost per million tokens.

prerequisites.en: Python — confident; asyncio basics help (we write load generators).
Linux command line and git — you will ship a repository every week (uv is shown in seminar 1).
Deep-learning basics — what a transformer forward pass and a token are; PyTorch at the reading level.
HTTP / REST basics — requests, JSON, streaming responses.
Accounts: GitHub, Hugging Face, Google (for Colab). No prior Docker or Kubernetes needed — taught in the course.

judge.en: The instructor's machine · 1 × NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti (Blackwell, 16 GB GDDR7), headless, nothing else running

devBox.en: Google Colab (free tier: NVIDIA T4, 16 GB)

modelRule.en: Any open-weight model that can serve the judge's load in 16 GB of VRAM: 64 concurrent requests × (512 prompt + 256 answer tokens) ≈ 49 000 tokens of KV cache next to the weights. Your choice — and it may change between rounds.

stackRule.en: Any stack and any kernels: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, TensorRT-LLM, your own CUDA/Triton — as long as the contract holds.

submission.en: Push a git tag round-NN (round-01 … round-10) to your public repository before Thursday 23:59. The judge checks out exactly that tag.

role.en: author, model (Hugging Face id), stack — printed on the board

from a clean checkout: install the pinned environment and start an OpenAI-compatible server on 0.0.0.0:8000, model name "submission", streaming /v1/chat/completions that honours max_tokens and ignore_eos and accepts requests of up to 4096 tokens (prompt + answer)
pinned environment (uv lock after every dependency change) — the run must be reproducible
one entry per round: what changed, why, what it measured — the raw material of your defense
optional — if present, the judge builds and runs it instead of serve.sh (must expose port 8000)

speed.en: Speed score S = geometric mean of output tokens/s at 32 and at 64 concurrent clients (GuideLLM · synthetic 512-token prompts → 256-token answers · prompts drawn with a secret seed).

quality.en: Quality gate: subsets of GSM8K, MMLU-Pro and IFEval through lm-eval against your endpoint. Each score must be ≥ 90% of the reference submission's score.

ranking.en: Among submissions that pass every gate, rank by S.

marks.en: mark = 5 × min(1, S / S_bar) if every gate passes, else 0. Each round is worth 4% of the course grade: points = mark × 0.8.

overdrive.en: Among submissions that cleared the bar (S ≥ S_bar): the top 10% get +2 Overdrive, the next 10% get +1 (rounded up; at least one student in each band; ties share).

exemption.en: Overdrive ≥ 10 after round 10 → the final exam is waived and credited at 40 / 50. The defense is still mandatory.

deadline.en: Every round closes on Thursday at 23:59.

latency.en: Latency gate: p95 time-to-first-token at 64 clients must not exceed the round's SLO (reference p95 × 1.25). Errors ≤ 1%, and answers must really be 256 tokens long.

thresholds.en: The quality gates, the speed bar S_bar and the latency SLO are re-published every week, before the round opens. Round 1 bars come from the reference submission (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct on vLLM) measured on Colab T4.

dryRun.en: Every Tuesday the judge dry-runs the current default branch of every repository (contract, start-up, smoke test on the RTX 5070 Ti) and publishes the logs — so you can see your submission start on Blackwell before Thursday.

canaryRule.en: Same-model check: hidden canary prompts are answered at rest and again under load; the answers must match (similarity ≥ 0.5). Serving a different model under load fails the round.

note.en: Covers all 15 topics, including multi-GPU and Kubernetes. Waived for Overdrive ≥ 10 (credited 40 / 50).
Mandatory. The engineering story of your solution: every change, why, and what it measured.

policy.en: Cheating — zero tolerance. No late submissions: a round closes on Thursday at 23:59; a missing tag is a 0 for that round. Gaming the benchmark (caching eval answers, special-casing the prompt set, degrading output to win speed) disqualifies the round.
